instruction:
An organic-food importer is screening certification options for a Chilean supplier. Perform a document-based scope check of the control-body recognitions newly inserted by Annex I of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2140. Consider only those new entries and their Chile recognition codes; exclude the corrections in Annex II and any pre-existing recognitions. Apply the exception markers in the new entries. This is a comparison of the published original texts: use the original EU–Chile agreement on trade in organic products and the original Annex I country-recognition list in Regulation (EU) 2021/2325 for the referenced equivalence conditions. Ignore subsequent amendments. We are testing the scope of these specified recognitions, not every possible route by which a shipment could enter the EU.

For each hypothetical lot below, determine (1) whether that lot falls within the EU's recognition of Chilean products under the specified agreement, including its product and origin conditions, and (2) all Chile control-body codes among the new entries whose category scope remains available for that lot after applying the exception markers. An empty set means no code within this restricted candidate set; it does not mean all imports are prohibited.

Treat the supplied tariff headings and Article 35(7) product categories as facts. All lots meet the relevant organic-production requirements; all Chile production/processing and ingredient origins are exactly as stated. No other ingredient or origin is involved. A statement that a control body is EU-recognised does not assert anything additional about recognition of its country's regime. No need to assess certificates, labelling, or whether a body would commercially accept the client.

Inventory (HS heading; category):
L1: Unprocessed mate leaves grown and harvested in Chile (0903; A).
L2: Live grapevine planting material propagated in Chile (0602; A).
L3: Pure beeswax produced in Chile, not a formulated cosmetic (1521; G).
L4: Pure essential oil distilled in Chile from Chile-grown plants, intended solely for non-food use (3301; G).
L5: Pure essential oil distilled in Chile from Chile-grown plants, intended for use as food (3301; G).
L6: Jam processed in Chile using only Chilean fruit and organic sugar imported from France under the EU organic regime (2007; D).
L7: Jam processed in Chile using only Chilean fruit and organic sugar produced in and imported directly from Peru under an EU-recognised control-body regime (2007; D).
L8: Whole unprocessed farmed salmon raised in Chile; not caught wild (0302; C).
L9: Grape wine made in Chile exclusively from Chile-grown grapes (2204; F).

Return only a table with one row per lot in L1–L9 order:
lot | agreement_covered | eligible_control_body_codes
Use YES or NO for agreement_covered. For the last column give the complete set of Chile recognition codes, separated by semicolons, or NONE for the empty set. Code order within a cell does not matter. Do not substitute missing information for NONE.

Suggested method: close the candidate set first, read the category and exception marks together, then follow the exception to the applicable agreement direction and its conditions before deciding eligibility for each lot.
